articles.title: cSINGV v1.0: development and evaluation of a 1.5 km coupled atmosphere–ocean–wave modelling system for the Western Maritime Continent
articles.titleEn: cSINGV v1.0: development and evaluation of a 1.5 km coupled atmosphere–ocean–wave modelling system for the Western Maritime Continent
articles.abstract: This study presents cSINGV v1.0, a high-resolution (1.5 km) regional coupled atmosphere–ocean–wave modelling system developed for the Western Maritime Continent (WMC), a region characterised by complex coastlines, shallow seas, and strong air–sea interactions. The system integrates a convection-permitting atmospheric model (SINGV) with newly configured ocean (NEMO) and wave (WAVEWATCH III) components within a unified coupling framework based on the Regional Coupled Suite and OASIS3-MCT coupler. Its primary contribution is the development of a fully coupled system that enables two-way interactions between atmosphere, ocean, and waves at kilometre scale. Before coupling, the ocean and wave components are configured in standalone mode for the WMC. The model is evaluated using a six-month simulation (January–June 2019) against multiple observational and reanalysis datasets. The ocean and wave components show good agreement with reference datasets, with sea surface temperature errors generally below 0.5 °C and significant wave height errors around 0.2 m. This agreement is maintained in the fully coupled configuration. The influence of coupling is assessed by comparing the coupled and uncoupled atmospheric configurations. Results show that coupling improves the spatial organisation of precipitation, the diurnal cycle over the ocean, and the offshore propagation of convection, while differences in near-surface atmospheric variables remain modest. Process-based analysis indicates that these improvements are primarily linked to enhanced latent heat flux driven by thermodynamic air–sea feedbacks associated with sea surface temperature variability. Case studies of individual Sumatra squall events further suggest that coupling may influence the organisation and persistence of eastward-propagating convection. The magnitude of this influence appears to depend on the dominant convective regime, although a larger sample of events is needed to confirm this dependence. Overall, cSINGV provides a physically consistent framework for representing coupled processes in the WMC and a useful platform for investigating air–sea–wave interactions at convection-permitting scales.

Overall, cSINGV provides a physically consistent framework for representing coupled processes in the WMC and a useful platform for investigating air–sea–wave interactions at convection-permitting scales.

articles.title: Past and future projected radiative effects from irrigation
articles.titleEn: Past and future projected radiative effects from irrigation
articles.abstract: Irrigation is the most dominant freshwater use practice on Earth, yet its effect on the top-of-atmosphere (TOA) radiative budget remains uncertain because past estimates have relied on idealised experiments or single-model frameworks. Here, we use historical simulations (1902–2014) from the Irrigation Model Intercomparison Project (IRRMIP) to provide the first multi-model quantification of irrigation-induced effective radiative forcing (ERF), defined as the change in net TOA radiative flux including rapid atmospheric adjustments. Across seven Earth system models, under prescribed sea surface temperatures (SST), the global multi-model mean (MMM) irrigation-induced ERF is positive but small (∼ 0.023 W m −2 ). While the global signal is small, it masks regional heterogeneity: South Asia and West Central Asia exhibit higher positive ERF (∼0.23 W m −2 ), with spatial maps revealing coherent forcing hotspots of up to +5 W m −2 over the Indo-Gangetic Plain that are consistent across all models, while East Asia shows negative ERF (∼-0.03 W m −2 ). The clear-sky ERF is greater than the all-sky ERF in most of the regions, indicating that cloud adjustments following irrigation may exert a negative contribution to the ERF. Correlations between historical irrigation ERF variability and its potential drivers suggest that reduced outgoing longwave radiation is the dominant control at the global scale, as well as in South Asia and West Central Asia, while near-surface temperature, precipitable water, albedo, and cloud cover contribute with substantial regional and inter-model variability. We additionally examine future changes in net TOA radiation imbalance (Δ R n,TOA ) from a fully coupled CMIP-style model (SSP1-2.6 and SSP3-7.0, 2015–2070) to assess whether the historical ERF pattern persists under future irrigation. The global mean Δ R n,TOA is more positive under the high irrigation demand pathway (SSP3-7.0) than under SSP1-2.6, consistent with projected differences in irrigation expansion between scenarios. These results demonstrate that irrigation's radiative influence, while small in the global mean, is regionally substantial and scenario-dependent, with implications for the attribution of regional climate change and for the design of land-based mitigation trajectories.

articles.title: CFDID: a China Flood Disaster Impact Database from 1994 to 2023
articles.titleEn: CFDID: a China Flood Disaster Impact Database from 1994 to 2023
articles.abstract: China is one of the countries most severely affected by flood disasters. Long-term and systematic flood impact data are essential for flood risk assessment, flood impact model calibration, disaster prevention and reduction. However, an open, long-term, China-focused event-scale database with detailed flood disaster impact indicators remains lacking. Here we present the China Flood Disaster Impact Database (CFDID), which contains 1716 flood disaster event records from 1994 to 2023, including 1391 parent-event (L1) records. CFDID is compiled from 66 official documents and covers five flood-related disaster categories: rainstorm flood, typhoon, snowmelt flood, ice-jam flood, and dam-break flood. Each record includes date, location, disaster category, data source and available values for eight impact indicators: deaths and missing persons, affected population, affected cropland area, damaged cropland area, failed cropland area, collapsed dwellings, damaged dwellings, and direct economic losses. The database was constructed using a workflow that combines optical character recognition (OCR), large language model (LLM)-based information extraction, and manual verification, thereby improving the efficiency of converting unstructured text information into structured event records while ensuring data quality. Relative to the corresponding official national totals during 1994–2023, the impacts reported in L1 records in CFDID account for 68.49 % of deaths and missing persons, 72.24 % of affected population, 60.70 % of affected cropland area, 65.67 % of collapsed dwellings, and 74.86 % of direct economic losses. Compared with commonly used international flood impact databases, CFDID contains more detailed event records and accounts for higher percentages of the corresponding official totals for most impact indicators. CFDID also includes agricultural impact indicators, which are rarely available in international hazard impact databases. CFDID is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22918521 (Cui et al., 2026) and will be continuously updated by year.

articles.title: Age of smoke sampled by aircraft during FIREX-AQ: methods and critical evaluation
articles.titleEn: Age of smoke sampled by aircraft during FIREX-AQ: methods and critical evaluation
articles.abstract: The age of smoke, meaning the time elapsed since it was produced in a fire, is an important parameter for interpreting measurements of evolving smoke composition. This study describes the smoke age estimates developed for large plumes sampled in the 2019 NASA-NOAA FIREX-AQ field experiment. Smoke ages are computed using two methods and applied to observations from two aircraft: the NASA DC-8 and NOAA Chemistry Twin Otter. The first method uses measurements of mean horizontal wind speed, as observed by the sampling aircraft, and distance to the fire to provide a single age estimate for each plume-crossing performed by the aircraft. While this “mean-wind method” uses accurate wind measurements, it can be systematically biased by assumptions that plume rise time is negligible and that winds are homogeneous horizontally and in time during the plume transport. Wind inhomogeneities due to terrain effects and day-to-night transition, among other factors, affected some plumes during FIREX-AQ. The mean-wind method therefore performs best for short-range transport over level terrain with steady winds. The second method relies on upwind air parcel trajectories and plume rise computed with multiple high-resolution meteorological datasets. This “trajectory-based method” quantifies age uncertainty from the meteorological ensemble, plume rise speed, wind speed errors, and fire location. The second method also resolves age differences from the center to edge of a transect. Still, it is susceptible to errors in the meteorological model. With careful comparison of the simulated trajectories to smoke transport observed from geostationary satellite imagery described here, we filter out many trajectory errors and improve the smoke age estimates. Across the two aircraft, the dataset provides ages for over 43 h (815 transects) of in situ measurements in smoke plumes from 115 different fires, with smoke ages ranging from 1 min to 40 h. The two age methods are strongly correlated ( R = 0.89) for the periods during FIREX-AQ when both ages are available. The mean-wind age is systematically 12 % younger than the trajectory-based age and the median absolute difference between them is 15 % (21 % for mean). The favorable agreement between the two age methods reflects that the mean-wind method was selectively applied to plumes with little wind variability. Trajectory-based ages are available for more of the FIREX-AQ smoke observations than the mean-wind ages. The median trajectory-based age uncertainty during FIREX-AQ is 24 % and the mean uncertainty is 37 %, due to a long-tailed distribution. The main source of age uncertainty is spread within the meteorological ensemble, followed by discrepancy between measured and modeled wind speed, then other factors like plume rise. The age uncertainty variable enables the user to identify periods with high or low confidence in the age estimate, thereby informing studies of smoke aging. Smoke ages data are available at https://doi.org/10.5067/ASDC/FIREXAQ_MetNav_ AircraftInSitu_DC8_Data_1 (Bennett et al., 2020) for the NASA DC-8 and https://doi.org/10.5067/ASDC/SUBORBITAL/ FIREXAQ_Analysis_N48_Data_1 (Holmes, 2021a) for the NOAA Chemistry Twin Otter.

articles.title: Compounding Human and Bioclimatic Factors Driving the Global Fire Crisis
articles.titleEn: Compounding Human and Bioclimatic Factors Driving the Global Fire Crisis
articles.abstract: Over millennia, social and ecological systems have been shaped by fire and have in turn shaped fire regimes. However, recent decades have seen an escalating “fire crisis” characterized by an increasing incidence of large, intense wildfires, most notably in forests. Voices in the academic literature and media often attribute the fire crisis to a narrow range of mechanisms, for example, fuel management or climate change. This failure to acknowledge the complexity of causes leads to simplistic framings of risk, and ultimately, proposed solutions that are either not feasible or may lead to undesired outcomes. In this review we outline the human and bioclimatic factors that are driving this fire crisis. Factors reviewed include the impacts of colonial legacies, which disrupted Indigenous land stewardship and traditional burning practices over centuries; policies of fire suppression; population growth, urbanization and land management practices; biotic disturbances such as insect outbreaks and invasive plant species; and climate change, which is affecting both fire regimes and social‐ecological resilience to fire. Many of these factors co‐occur leading to complex interactions and, often, unexpected outcomes. Our review highlights that climate change is now having a compounding effect, building on a multitude of other factors to drive the fire crisis. Addressing this crisis requires first acknowledging its complexity and moving beyond simple framings of risk. We suggest solutions will vary across different places and through time, but may include supporting Indigenous land stewardship, adopting flexible fire responses, shifting societal expectations from aggressive fire suppression to “living with fire”, and fostering resilient social and ecological communities.

articles.title: Revealing the Widespread Bias of Extinction Risk in the Antarctic and the Southern Ocean
articles.titleEn: Revealing the Widespread Bias of Extinction Risk in the Antarctic and the Southern Ocean
articles.abstract: Accelerating environmental change in the Antarctic and Southern Ocean (ASO) necessitates robust extinction risk assessments to inform conservation priorities. Nevertheless, no systematic, region‐wide baseline of extinction risk currently exists for tracking ASO biodiversity responses to ongoing change, a significant barrier to global biodiversity monitoring. Here, we conducted the first ASO‐wide synthesis of current extinction risk knowledge for plants, animals and Fungi. This included examining biases in current assessments, the distribution of Threatened species and their associated threats. Using a data‐inclusive workflow, we compiled 8908 assessments representing 4970 species, more than doubling the number of ASO species assessed compared with any single source. As expected, assessments were heavily biased towards vertebrates (58% assessed), while invertebrates, despite their ecological prevalence, were markedly underrepresented (6% assessed). Among vertebrates, mammals had the highest proportion of Threatened species (26%). Birds within the ASO were disproportionately Threatened (25%) compared to the global average (11%), with the greatest threat for ASO species being ‘Biological Resource Use’. The sub‐Antarctic Islands had the highest density of both Threatened species and assessment effort, whereas many Antarctic species remain unassessed. Additionally, Threatened species have the lowest protected area coverage of any conservation status. These pronounced assessment biases highlight the need for more balanced, representative and data‐inclusive extinction risk assessments to be able to effectively detect conservation status change. This work represents an important step in ensuring ASO representation in global biodiversity monitoring frameworks, strengthening the capacity of these frameworks to detect, attribute and respond to future biodiversity changes.

articles.title: When Drought Is Not Drought: How Metrics Bias Estimates of Ecosystem Water Limitation
articles.titleEn: When Drought Is Not Drought: How Metrics Bias Estimates of Ecosystem Water Limitation
articles.abstract: Anthropogenic warming and shifts in global precipitation regimes are increasing rainfall variability and the frequency of intense precipitation events, raising uncertainty about how conventional meteorological drought indices capture ecosystem water limitation. This uncertainty arises from two key issues: temporal aggregation, as most meteorological drought indices are based on monthly integrated summaries, and drought definition, because atmospheric water deficits do not necessarily translate into vegetation water stress. Here, we quantified ecosystem gross primary productivity (GPP) responses to drought using three approaches: (1) monthly meteorological drought identified from monthly standardized precipitation evaporation index (SPEI), (2) daily meteorological drought defined by daily SPEI, and (3) ecological drought defined using an indicator of actual vegetation water limitation. Comparing monthly and daily SPEI‐based drought isolated the effects of temporal aggregation, while comparing daily meteorological and ecological droughts quantified the influence of drought definition. Across 130 eddy‐covariance sites spanning multiple biomes and climate zones, we analyzed 6691 drought months identified using monthly SPEI. Daily SPEI data revealed that within months classified as meteorological drought, nearly 50% of days did not coincide with atmospheric water deficits owing to daily rainfall variability. As a result, monthly SPEI overestimated GPP responses (20.60% ± 5.28% increase) relative to daily SPEI (4.61% ± 1.21% increase). In contrast, daily meteorological drought metrics underestimated drought‐induced suppression of GPP by ~46% compared with ecological drought, demonstrating that atmospheric drought metrics do not fully reflect water stress experienced by vegetation. Our results show that both temporal resolution and drought definition can bias estimates of ecosystem drought responses, underscoring the need for finer‐scale temporal and ecologically relevant measures of vegetation water limitation to improve understanding of biosphere–climate interactions in an increasingly drought‐prone world.

articles.title: Climate‐Driven Oceanographic Changes Shape Larval Dispersal Success in the Southern Ocean
articles.titleEn: Climate‐Driven Oceanographic Changes Shape Larval Dispersal Success in the Southern Ocean
articles.abstract: Although climate‐driven changes in ocean circulation are increasingly recognized as key drivers of marine ecosystem structure and dynamics, their consequences for the early life stages of deep‐sea fishes remain difficult to quantify. In the Southern Ocean, variability in frontal systems such as the Polar Front (PF) may influence larval dispersal and retention, with direct implications for recruitment. We investigated how interannual variability in ocean circulation and egg production shapes larval dispersal and retention in suitable recruitment areas of a large body size deep‐sea fish species, Patagonian toothfish ( Dissostichus eleginoides ), around the Kerguelen Plateau. We developed an integrated modeling framework which combined spatially explicit models of egg production with 24 years (2000–2023) of Lagrangian dispersal simulations driven by satellite‐derived geostrophic currents to quantify successful larval retention. Ontogenetic changes in distribution and fecundity were accounted for to model egg production, allowing retention metrics to reflect spatial heterogeneity in reproductive output. Larval retention rate in suitable recruitment areas varied from 9% to 28% over the study period. PF‐associated jet intensity was significantly associated with larval retention variability: years characterized by stronger PF‐associated circulation showed lower larval retention, with more larvae advected away from the shelf toward the eastern part of the plateau. The latter part of the time series, particularly after 2010, was characterized by stronger year‐to‐year fluctuations, a higher contribution of the North‐West recruitment area, and more frequent low‐retention years. Building on new findings on toothfish spawning dynamics and long‐term altimetry data, we showed for the first time that there is the potential for self‐recruitment in the northern part of the Kerguelen Plateau (French EEZ). We also discussed the implications for fishery management since PF‐associated indices may help interpret past recruitment trends and offer useful early‐warning for future recruitment anomalies.

articles.title: Dual Constraints of Microbial Carbon Use Efficiency and Mineral Protection Govern Necromass Accrual
articles.titleEn: Dual Constraints of Microbial Carbon Use Efficiency and Mineral Protection Govern Necromass Accrual
articles.abstract: Increasing soil organic carbon (SOC), central to food security and climate mitigation, is increasingly recognized as being mediated by microbial necromass C (MNC) accrual. However, how microbial production and mineral preservation jointly govern MNC accrual under contrasting resource conditions remains unclear. Here, we analyzed soils from 14 long‐term fertilization experiments (up to 47 years) to assess how edaphic and climatic conditions regulate the response of MNC accrual to manure (M) and non‐manure (NM) fertilization treatments. We found that the primary constraints on MNC accrual varied with resource availability, with microbial production under resource‐limited conditions and mineral preservation under resource‐abundant conditions. Under resource‐limited conditions, M treatments increased MNC by up to 122%, with changes tightly coupled to SOC gains. This accrual was associated with increases in dissolved organic C and microbial C use efficiency, indicating a production‐constrained pathway in which manure inputs alleviate substrate limitation and promote microbial C allocation toward biomass production and necromass formation. Conversely, under resource‐abundant conditions, MNC responses to fertilization were weaker (+56%) and uncoupled from SOC gains. Instead, MNC accrual was primarily associated with mineral protection capacity (e.g., Fe and Al oxides), consistent with a preservation‐constrained pathway. Overall, microbial processing and mineral preservation represent context‐dependent constraints on MNC accrual under contrasting resource conditions. These findings underscore the importance of resource context for site‐specific C management and for understanding soil C dynamics under global change.

articles.title: Quantifying the impact of groundwater fauna and temperature on the ecosystem service of microbial carbon degradation; a proof-of-principle approach
articles.titleEn: Quantifying the impact of groundwater fauna and temperature on the ecosystem service of microbial carbon degradation; a proof-of-principle approach
articles.abstract: Groundwater ecosystems fulfil functions that humankind relies upon, e.g. for sustainable drinking water production. Quantification of these services is lacking so far. Thus, it is not possible to predict scenarios (e.g. future climates). Based on data from a comprehensive groundwater ecosystem study comprising four zones of varying land use and groundwater/surface water exchange, we parameterized a quantitative dynamic food web model (recharged organic carbon, microorganisms using the biodegradable fraction of this carbon, and fauna grazing on the microorganisms), in a proof-of-principle approach. With the model satisfactorily reflecting the field data, we calculated five further scenarios, three of which without fauna (mortality e.g. due to contamination, sudden peaks of temperature etc.). Two of the “fauna” and two of the “no fauna” scenarios were run with temperature elevated by 1.5 and 3 °C, respectively. The ecosystem service of carbon degradation was expressed as the difference in carbon concentration between the beginning of the simulation and the end of the simulation. In most scenarios, remaining carbon increased over time. The remaining carbon in some scenarios was up to 6.6 times as high in the “no fauna” scenarios compared to the reference case. Fauna was thus shown to fulfil a service by promoting microbial carbon degradation that may be substantial. This model set up can serve to test other cases of varying physical and chemical variations and disturbances.

Two of the “fauna” and two of the “no fauna” scenarios were run with temperature elevated by 1.5 and 3 °C, respectively. The ecosystem service of carbon degradation was expressed as the difference in carbon concentration between the beginning of the simulation and the end of the simulation. In most scenarios, remaining carbon increased over time. The remaining carbon in some scenarios was up to 6.6 times as high in the “no fauna” scenarios compared to the reference case. Fauna was thus shown to fulfil a service by promoting microbial carbon degradation that may be substantial. articles.title: Riverine biogeochemistry from the Andes to the ocean: longitudinal patterns along a Mediterranean Andean catchment in central Chile
articles.titleEn: Riverine biogeochemistry from the Andes to the ocean: longitudinal patterns along a Mediterranean Andean catchment in central Chile
articles.abstract: Rivers act as dynamic connectors between terrestrial and marine ecosystems, transporting and transforming materials along the aquatic continuum. We investigated longitudinal biogeochemical patterns across the Rapel catchment (central Chile) by integrating dissolved organic matter (DOM) characterization, dissolved metals and nutrients, and microbial community profiling from the Andean headwaters to the Pacific Ocean. Headwaters were characterized by low DOC and nutrient concentrations, high protein-like fluorescence, and diverse microbial assemblages dominated by Flavobacterium, Polaromonas, and Rhodoferax. Downstream, agricultural and mining activities increased nutrient and metal concentrations and altered microbial community composition with an increasing prevalence of hgcI_clade. The Rapel Reservoir emerged as a major biogeochemical discontinuity, promoting DOM transformation, restructuring microbial assemblages, and modifying downstream chemical conditions. Overall, tributary inputs, land use, and hydrological regulation disrupted simple longitudinal patterns and generated distinct biogeochemical processing zones. These findings highlight the interplay between downstream transport and local processing in shaping riverine functioning in Mediterranean Andean catchments and provide a basis for assessing future climate and land-use impacts on riverine biogeochemistry.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal variations of carbon-water-hydraulic risk for Pinus tabuliformis Carrière Plantations on the Loess Plateau under future climate change
articles.titleEn: Spatiotemporal variations of carbon-water-hydraulic risk for Pinus tabuliformis Carrière Plantations on the Loess Plateau under future climate change
articles.abstract: As a native perennial tree, Pinus tabuliformis Carrière (PT) has been widely planted on the Chinese Loess Plateau for ecological restoration. However, the impacts of climate-change on water resources pose a new challenge to the sustainability of restored ecosystems. To clarify the plantation carbon sequestration and water consumption, as well as their underlying physiological mechanisms, this study coupled the integrated BBGC-Sperry model with CMIP6 meteorological data under SSP1–2.6, SSP2–4.5, and SSP5–8.5. Daily transpiration, soil water content, and leaf water potential, along with multi-site total growing-season transpiration and aboveground biomass data, were used to validate the BBGC-Sperry model. The validated model was used to simulate the dynamics of annual mean NPP, annual mean actual evapotranspiration (ET) and annual average percentage loss of whole-plant hydraulic conductance (APLK) for PT plantations at 130 meteorological stations on the Loess Plateau. We integrated a “carbon-water-hydraulic risk index” (CWHRI) based on NPP, ET, and drought-induced mortality risk probability (DMRP) to assess ecosystem sustainability. These simulations covered the baseline period (2000–2024) and three future periods (2025–2049, NFP; 2050–2074, MFP; and 2075–2099, FFP) under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1–2.6, SSP2–4.5, and SSP5–8.5). The results indicate that compared with the baseline period, the annual mean NPP is projected to decrease by 4 %–27 % under all scenario–period combinations, except for the FFP under SSP5–8.5, where it will increase by 8 %. Annual mean ET and APLK are projected to increase from 0.05 %–61 % and 13 %–84 %, respectively, with the smallest increases under SSP1–2.6 with the NFP and the largest under SSP5–8.5 with the FFP. The CWHRI is projected to decline by 23 %–44 %, and exhibit a southeast-to-northwest decreasing gradient, which is dominated by NPP, with a secondary contribution from water-related environmental factors. These findings indicate the rising DMRP of PT plantations will threaten the sustainability of restored ecosystems on the Loess Plateau in the future.

articles.title: Divergent mercury accumulation dynamics in tropical dry and moist broadleaf forests
articles.titleEn: Divergent mercury accumulation dynamics in tropical dry and moist broadleaf forests
articles.abstract: Forests are major sinks for atmospheric mercury (Hg) due to the efficiency of stomatal uptake and litter deposition. Tropical forests, highly productive ecosystems, remain understudied despite their pronounced climatic and phenological variability. We investigated whether seasonal rainfall regimes and associated tree adaptations influence Hg dynamics in secondary tropical moist broadleaf (TMBF) and tropical dry broadleaf (TDBF) forests in Costa Rica by examining foliar Hg concentrations, litter Hg standing stocks, and soil Hg concentrations. Seasonal differences in rainfall and associated environmental conditions strongly influenced foliar Hg concentration in the TDBF. Deciduous trees showed 4.7 times higher foliar Hg concentration in the wet season, when leaves were mature, compared to the dry season, when newly flushed leaves emerged after leaf shedding. Evergreen trees in TDBF demonstrated 2.3 times lower foliar Hg concentrations in the dry season than in the wet season (23 vs. 53 µg kg −1 ), likely due to various associated physiological processes (e.g., leaf flushing). However, the primary mechanism remains unclear given the complex and unexplored Hg dynamics in TDBF. TMBF showed no clear seasonal variation in foliar Hg in either deciduous (dry: 48; wet: 54 µg kg −1 ) or evergreen trees (dry: 57; wet: 53 µg kg −1 ), likely due to longer leaf lifespan sustaining year-round transpiration and stomatal Hg uptake under high humidity. Atmospheric Hg concentrations in TDBF were two times higher than in TMBF (1.2 vs. 0.7 ng m −3 ) across both seasons, likely reflecting greater Hg capture per unit area in TMBF due to denser vegetation and enhanced wet deposition via rainfall. Foliar Hg was not correlated with stomatal density or specific leaf area in either forest type. Soil Hg concentrations, however, were correlated with litter-derived inputs, supporting litter as the dominant Hg transfer pathway. Higher seasonally averaged litter Hg standing stocks (34 µg m −2 ) in TMBF than in the TDBF (19 µg m −2 ) resulted in 3.4 times higher soil Hg concentrations (0–30 cm) in TMBF (115 µg kg −1 ) than in TDBF (34 µg kg −1 ). Soil Hg concentrations were 2.6 times lower at a previously deforested TMBF site, indicating persistent disturbance effects despite almost three decades of reforestation. Overall, foliar Hg concentrations in the TDBF varied markedly between seasons, while both TDBF and TMBF appeared to be important Hg 0 reservoirs, with contrasting dynamics that are potentially sensitive to climate change.

articles.title: Improved permafrost soil representation in a dynamic global vegetation model enhances simulations of carbon dynamics and vegetation structure in boreal forests of Northeast China
articles.titleEn: Improved permafrost soil representation in a dynamic global vegetation model enhances simulations of carbon dynamics and vegetation structure in boreal forests of Northeast China
articles.abstract: Boreal forests play an important role in the global terrestrial carbon cycle, yet the effects of climate-driven permafrost degradation on ecosystem carbon dynamics remain poorly represented in current models. Earth system models often simplify subsurface thermal and hydrological processes, limiting their ability to capture ecosystem responses in permafrost-affected regions. Here, we improve the soil module of the LPJ-GUESS model by implementing a deep soil profile (3 m) with refined vertical discretization (30 layers) and explicit ice-impedance effects. The improved LPJ-GUESS configuration is then applied to simulate carbon and hydrothermal dynamics in the climate-sensitive boreal forests of Northeast China. Model evaluation indicates that the improved configuration generally enhances the simulation of soil hydrothermal dynamics relative to the default LPJ-GUESS configuration. The correlation coefficient for deep soil temperature (1.0 m) increases from 0.818 to 0.894, while the systematic overestimation of soil water content is substantially reduced, with the bias at 1.0 m reduced from 0.321 to −0.006. These improvements are associated with better agreement between simulated and observed vegetation composition. The simulated dominance of needleleaf forests decreases from near-complete dominance to 24.1 %, resulting in vegetation patterns that are more consistent with regional observations. Consequently, biases in carbon estimates are reduced, with simulated net primary productivity decreasing from 583.5 to 560.1 g C m −2 yr −1 and aboveground biomass from 112.9 to 99.0 t ha −1 , resulting in better agreement with estimates from satellite-based observations. Model sensitivity analysis indicates that vegetation composition is highly sensitive to changes in soil hydrothermal conditions compared with the control simulation. Pronounced shifts in vegetation composition occur when soil temperature increases exceed 0.6 °C and soil water deficits exceed 0.6 m 3 m −3 compared to the default model configuration. Overall, this study highlights the importance of improving soil hydrothermal representation for simulating vegetation dynamics and carbon cycling in permafrost-affected boreal ecosystems.

articles.title: Composition, frequency, and severity of future rain-on-snow floods in Germany
articles.titleEn: Composition, frequency, and severity of future rain-on-snow floods in Germany
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: In Germany, severe widespread winter floods are often generated by rain-on-snow (ROS) phenomena. Under suitable conditions, when rain falls on the snow cover, the snow can melt and produce extreme amounts of runoff. In a warming climate, the frequency of ROS events is expected to change locally depending on elevation and regionally based on the general climate conditions. Consequently, the characteristics of ROS-driven winter floods are also anticipated to change. To investigate these changes, streamflow for multiple gauge stations in Germany was simulated using an ensemble of Long Short-Term Memory models based on an ensemble of downscaled climate projections. Germany, as a representative mid-latitude country with a considerable portion of historical floods generated by ROS, offers extensive spatial and temporal coverage of hydrological observations spanning long temporal scales, and hence warranting efficient training of the deep learning model. We used an explainable artificial intelligence method, integrated gradients, to examine flood-generating processes, focusing primarily on ROS, for every simulated flood peak. Changes in frequency, feature importance, and a ranking based severity of ROS flood events were assessed for individual streamflow gauges and for widespread floods affecting multiple catchments across four major river basins in Germany. We found that with regard to the ensemble median, the frequency of ROS floods will mostly decrease at the scale of individual gauges by up to 60 %, as well as at the widespread scale for the Rhine, Elbe, and Weser River basins but increase at gauges located in the Danube River basin for the corresponding widespread floods. For all regions, the snowmelt component during ROS floods becomes less relevant, whereas the contribution of rainfall to these events increases. Interestingly, the severity of the mean and the most extreme widespread ROS floods is projected to increase compared to the historical period in all major river basins in Germany. Only for individual gauges the severity may decrease in the future. Despite the overall agreement in the trends of the input features across climate models, the resulting trends in ROS floods are considerably disparate. This discrepancy is primarily attributed to complex model chains in the climate models leading to variability in rainfall and snowmelt, and to different melting seasons.

articles.title: Towards improved integration of hydrological uncertainty and hydraulic model sensitivity in flood hazard mapping
articles.titleEn: Towards improved integration of hydrological uncertainty and hydraulic model sensitivity in flood hazard mapping
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: The study presents a novel framework for integrating hydrological uncertainties and the related sensitivity of the hydrodynamic modelling results into flood hazard mapping. Uncertainties in flood frequency analysis (FFA), including anticipated impact of climate change and sensitivity to channel and floodplain roughness, were examined through selected scenario ensembles. The study area is the lower Vipava river, a transboundary catchment shared between Slovenia and Italy with variable floodplain topography. Sensitivity analysis revealed that uncertainty in FFA and river channel roughness significantly influenced the inundation spatial extent and inundation depth, the impact of floodplain roughness appears to be limited. The analysis shows that natural successional changes in river channel roughness substantially impact the results of a 10 year return period (RP) event, increasing flood extent by 45 %. The increase in inundated areas is less pronounced for 100 and 500 year RP floods, with increases of 15 % and 11 %, respectively. The weighted exceedance probability of inundation (WEPI) based on scenario ensembles provided an informative identification of areas most susceptible to potential changes in flood hazard. Our results highlight the value of targeted scenario ensembles that incorporate FFA uncertainty and hydraulic roughness sensitivity, thereby producing more informative flood hazard mapping that can complement deterministic mapping approaches and support more adaptive future land use planning.

articles.title: From forecast to alert: an open-data AI flood early warning system with reservoir monitoring for the White Volta Basin
articles.titleEn: From forecast to alert: an open-data AI flood early warning system with reservoir monitoring for the White Volta Basin
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Flood early warning in the White Volta Basin of northern Ghana is complicated by unmonitored dam releases from Burkina Faso's Bagre Reservoir, which existing globally calibrated systems do not represent. We present an end-to-end AI-driven flood early warning system that integrates observed gauge discharge, CHIRPS satellite rainfall, ERA5-Land reanalysis forcing, and a novel JRC-derived Bagre reservoir storage proxy. An ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM models trained on these inputs achieved Kling–Gupta Efficiency scores of 0.984, 0.974, and 0.957 at 1, 3, and 5 d lead times on an independent test period dominated by moderate flows (maximum 1206 m 3 s −1 , below the Orange alert threshold); higher-tier alert skill rests on leave-one-year-out cross-validation rather than held-out extreme events. Benchmarking against simple baselines shows the ensemble's advantage over a persistence forecast is marginal at 1 d lead but grows with lead time and concentrates on rising-limb and high-flow conditions, indicating that recent observed discharge carries most of the short-range skill while the ensemble's value lies at the longer horizons relevant to warning. For direct comparison, GloFAS v4 reanalysis discharge at Nawuni achieves KGE = −0.526 on the same test period, performing worse than a climatological mean predictor, primarily because LISFLOOD does not represent Bagre Dam release operations. A four-tier alert system calibrated to 30-year flood return periods achieved a cross-validated Red-tier probability of detection of 0.902 (false alarm ratio 0.134) at 1 d lead, declining to 0.762 at 5 d. Sentinel-1 SAR mapping provided spatial grounding for the discharge-based threshold framework, with Red-tier exceedance periods associated with floodplain inundation extents of 50 to 149 km 2 across three validation seasons. The system integrates into Ghana's existing myDEWETRA-VOLTALARM platform without requiring new institutional infrastructure. The Bagre reservoir proxy, derived from freely available JRC Global Surface Water imagery and validated against independent satellite altimetry ( r = 0.94), provides a measure of reservoir state. Because the reservoir fills to capacity in most wet seasons, this signal functions as an explicit model input and as seasonal situational awareness that the reservoir is capable of spilling, rather than as a standalone flood trigger.

articles.title: Comparing and validating modelled snow stability metrics
articles.titleEn: Comparing and validating modelled snow stability metrics
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Recent developments in snow stability modelling demonstrated the great potential of numerical snow cover modelling for avalanche forecasting. These recently developed metrics provided promising results, possibly even superseding traditional stability indices. To further validate these results, we compared the temporal evolution of various stability metrics to a unique dataset of measurements, including snow stratigraphy, snow microstructure, and stability obtained at the high Alpine study site Steintälli above Davos (Eastern Swiss Alps) during the winter 2015/16. There, we measured the shear strength of a prominent weak layer of depth hoar crystals using the shear frame and assessed the propagation propensity of this weak layer with propagation saw tests. Concurrently, we characterized snow microstructure with the snow micro-penetrometer (SMP). At the study site, an automated weather station is located, providing the data to run the numerical snow cover model SNOWPACK so that modelled stability metrics can be derived. Field measurements showed that weak layer strength and toughness were initially low but increased over time, in parallel with the increasing slab load; all three parameters were correlated. While field observations focused on the most prominent weak layer, modelled stability metrics were evaluated for the persistent weak layers identified by the respective modelling approaches. These generally corresponded well to the layers visually identified in simulated snow stratigraphy. Data-driven and process-based stability metrics exhibited similar temporal evolution and comparable skill in relation to local avalanche activity, achieving overall accuracies of 53 %–68 %. This site-specific validation demonstrates that both types of numerical stability metrics provide valuable support for avalanche forecasting, although differences in their behaviour highlight the need for metric-specific interpretation. Hence, a multi-model approach may be advantageous for operational forecasting.

articles.title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
articles.titleEn: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
articles.abstract: In recent years, record-breaking heatwaves have occurred over many regions of the Earth causing serious impacts to human and natural systems. Here we show that recently observed exceptional heatwaves are no match to potential future 21 st century events based on multiple metrics. For several observed heatwaves, this holds even under low- and medium-emissions scenarios. In a high- to very high-emissions future, many regions are projected to experience heatwaves that generate several times more cumulative heat and are many times longer (up to several months) than the observed heatwaves. Should the Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement not be implemented, in most regions a concerningly large proportion of projected heatwaves exceeds all analyzed heatwave characteristics at once. Our results underscore the crucial need for substantial emissions reduction and have important implications for adaptation measures, as a substantial proportion of projected heatwaves is well outside the recent lived experience.

Our results underscore the crucial need for substantial emissions reduction and have important implications for adaptation measures, as a substantial proportion of projected heatwaves is well outside the recent lived experience.

articles.title: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
articles.titleEn: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
articles.abstract: The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. The tuning properties of neural populations collectively shift and rescale with the range. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

articles.title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
articles.titleEn: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
articles.abstract: X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. Here we show through start-to-end simulations how to realise compact, robust and tunable X-ray lasers in the water window, based on ultra-bright electron beams from plasma wakefield accelerators. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability – both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation.

articles.title: Molecular-level control of nitrogen sites enables CO2 electro-reduction under industrially relevant conditions
articles.titleEn: Molecular-level control of nitrogen sites enables CO2 electro-reduction under industrially relevant conditions
articles.abstract: Industrial flue gases typically contain only 3–15% CO 2 , and direct electrochemical reduction on such dilute feeds would eliminate costly upstream purification. However, mass transport limitations and competing hydrogen evolution severely restrict activity under these CO 2 -starved conditions, and the governing molecular factors remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that pyridinic-nitrogen enrichment in Ni–N–C single-atom catalysts enables efficient CO 2 reduction under dilute CO 2 . By tuning the pyridinic-N to pyrrolic-N ratio in well-defined Ni–N x sites, we probe the role of local nitrogen environments in CO 2 reduction rather than the metal center alone. Electronic-state analysis and density functional theory reveal that pyridinic-N forms a reversible CO 2 adduct that enhances local CO 2 accessibility near the active Ni center through a desorption–re-adsorption relay. These findings provide molecular-level insight by identifying a neighboring motif that regulates local CO 2 availability without perturbing the intrinsic Ni–N reaction pathway, and by establishing a transferable design principle for CO 2 reduction catalysts under CO 2 -limited conditions.

articles.title: Emissions Poised to Rocket: Modeling the Environmental Impacts of Low Earth Orbit Satellite Constellations
articles.titleEn: Emissions Poised to Rocket: Modeling the Environmental Impacts of Low Earth Orbit Satellite Constellations
articles.abstract: The proliferation of satellite megaconstellations in low Earth orbit represents a significant advancement in global broadband connectivity. However, we urgently need to understand the potential environmental impacts, particularly greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with these constellations. This study addresses a critical gap in modeling current and future GHG emissions by developing an open‐source life cycle assessment methodology, applied to 12 launch vehicles and 24 megaconstellations. Our analysis reveals that fully deploying the 24 constellations would emit about 9.1 Mt CO 2 . Propellant combustion during launch events (60.9%) and launcher production (31.6%) contribute most significantly to overall GHG emissions, accounting for 92.5% of modeled life cycle emissions. Reusing launch vehicles lowers production emissions per launch by 81%–97% relative to building a new vehicle for every flight, highlighting the environmental benefits of reusability in space technology. The findings underscore the importance of launch vehicle and satellite design choices to minimize potential environmental impacts. The Open‐source Rocket and Constellation Lifecycle Emissions (ORACLE) repository is freely available and aims to facilitate further research in this field. This study provides a critical baseline for policymakers and industry stakeholders to develop strategies for reducing the carbon footprint of the space industry, especially satellite megaconstellations.

articles.title: Projection of the Status and Future Shifts of Topsoil Organic Carbon Stocks in Northern Hemisphere Permafrost Regions: Patterns and Drivers
articles.titleEn: Projection of the Status and Future Shifts of Topsoil Organic Carbon Stocks in Northern Hemisphere Permafrost Regions: Patterns and Drivers
articles.abstract: The Northern Hemisphere (NH) permafrost areas harbor vast reservoirs of soil organic carbon (SOC), which are potentially at serious releasing risk due to climate change. However, projections of future changes in SOC stocks in these regions remain subject to large uncertainties. In this study, we constructed an integrated approach that combines space‐for‐time substitution with a machine learning model to estimate the current status of surface (0–30 cm) SOC stocks in NH permafrost regions and to project their future changes throughout the 21st century under various Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). The results indicate that approximately 224.2 Pg C were stored in NH permafrost regions during the baseline period (1981–2000), and they will remain relatively stable (−0.5% ± 0.9%) until the conclusion of 21st century under SSP1‐2.6, while a significant loss of about 8.5% ± 3.5% is projected under SSP5‐8.5. Spatially, the areas with increased surface SOC in the future are mainly located in the continuous permafrost zone, while the decrease is identified in most of discontinuous, sporadic, and isolated permafrost areas. Among ecosystems, grasslands and deserts are projected to act as future carbon sinks, while forests exhibit the largest declines. Temperature exerts the strongest control on SOC dynamics in the northern circumpolar (NC) permafrost region through a nonlinear threshold effect, whereas precipitation and vegetation productivity govern SOC changes in the Third Pole. These results highlight pronounced spatial heterogeneity of SOC dynamics in permafrost regions, providing valuable insights for carbon–climate feedback assessments and regional policy.

articles.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
articles.titleEn: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
articles.abstract: Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe’s Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age 1–3 . How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested 4 , with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. Here we analyse genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which these models fit reconstructed demographic histories. We identify three main processes shaping European population structure that are relevant to the Celtic dispersal. First, the arrival of Steppe-related ancestry with Bell Beaker-associated groups after around 4400 bp (calibrated years before present or 1950 ce ) across the region in which Celtic and related languages were later spoken. Second, a movement from southwestern Europe into Britain during the Bronze Age (3800–3200 bp ), consistent with scenarios in which Celtic formed along the Atlantic façade. Third, a westward expansion of ancestry related to Late Bronze Age Knovíz–Urnfield-associated populations from eastern central Europe (3200–2800 bp ), affecting France, the British Isles, northeastern Iberia and Italy and later associated with Iron Age Hallstatt and La Tène contexts 5–8 . Although all three movements have parallels with proposed models, we argue that the final movement, from eastern central Europe, is most parsimonious for the spread of Celtic. Although human history does not necessarily follow a parsimonious trajectory 9 and language shifts need not track genetic change, these results delimit the demographic scenarios that are plausible for the emergence of Celtic in prehistoric Europe.

articles.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
articles.titleEn: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
articles.abstract: Hydrogen-bearing materials are central to low-carbon energy technologies 1 , but hydrogen itself is difficult to detect and localize at the nanoscale 2–6 . This hinders the development of advanced materials with better efficiency. Atom probe tomography (APT) can map hydrogen in three dimensions and at high resolution, yet characterization of dilute, mobile, interstitial hydrogen in metals has remained challenging because of low solubility, the ambiguity owing to hydrogen trapping by structural defects, as well as the artefacts introduced during hydrogen introduction 4–6 . Here we address whether interstitial hydrogen in solution in materials can be distinguished from defect-trapped hydrogen in APT. Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, together with face-centred cubic (FCC) multi-principal-element alloys (MPEAs) containing coherent FCC precipitates, we show that deuterium atoms reproducibly concentrate in hydrogen-affinitive phases in a manner consistent with theoretical predictions. We further resolve differences in deuterium content between phases with distinct local chemistries and crystal structures, consistent with their different calculated hydrogen solution energies. These findings demonstrate that APT can move beyond identifying hydrides and solute-decorated defects to examine hydrogen in solid solution, providing new insights into hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys and informing materials design for hydrogen-related applications.

articles.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
articles.titleEn: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD 1–3 . Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge 4 . Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals 5 , and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts 6,7 ; however, the biological basis of this ‘female protective effect’ (FPE) has remained unknown 8,9 . Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that drive this transcriptomic convergence, including prominent ASD gene CHD8 and candidates including REST . Furthermore, X-linked transcription factor ZFX, which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in female individuals 10 , emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in the female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the female protective effect. Together, these results show how key gene regulatory networks can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.

articles.title: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling
articles.titleEn: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling
articles.abstract: The vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival 1 . Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF–VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells 2,3 . The anti-VEGF antibody, which can block angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or ischaemic diseases, is among the most widely used antibodies in the clinic. However, vascular resistance to anti-VEGF therapy has been reported 4,5 . Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe –HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. These Vegfr2 -knockout ( Vegfr2 KO ) ECs adapted, proliferated normally and competed with wild-type cells over time, eventually forming a substantial portion of the vascular network in most organs. Vegfr2 KO ECs could not sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because this process is highly VEGF-dependent and favours growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, owing to their inability to respond to VEGF, Vegfr2 KO ECs became dominant in veins, which represented a long-term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2 identified both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. These included significant endothelial venousization and upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 compensated only in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. Notably, loss of the master regulator of venous development, NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), significantly compromised expansion of Vegfr2 KO ECs. This work has implications for our understanding of the role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and demonstrates venousization as a mechanism of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss during angiogenesis.

articles.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
articles.titleEn: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
articles.abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au (ref. 1 ) but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation 2,3 , effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation 4 . Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation 5,6 . Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories 7 . Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) 8 to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) 9–11 coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2–15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b (ref. 12 ) at 4.3 μm. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

articles.title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
articles.titleEn: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
articles.abstract: First proposed by Milgrom in 1983 as an alternative to the standard Cold Dark Matter (CDM) paradigm, Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) has gained renewed momentum in light of persistent nondetections of exotic dark matter particles and growing tensions facing CDM on galactic scales. While MOND perfectly reproduces galactic rotation curves, it encounters notable challenges in explaining the equilibrium of galaxy clusters. Although it reduces the overall dark matter budget in these massive systems, an unidentified mass component remains required. This paper investigates the hypothesis that this missing mass is baryonic: composed of nonradiating ordinary matter such as stellar remnants, gas too diffuse to initiate star formation, or compact, ultra-dense clouds of cold molecular gas with low volume filling factors. Using a sample of 106 clusters mapped in X-rays, emitted by the hot intracluster medium composing most of the visible mass, we derive first the total mass within the Newtonian dynamics, assuming hydrostatic equilibrium and spherical symmetry. Then, with the modified Poisson equation, we reconstruct the spatial distribution of the invisible missing matter within the MOND framework. In the sample, the relaxed systems harboring cooling flows, known as cool-core clusters, have the highest peaks of dark missing mass. Its density profile reveals a pronounced central concentration bounded by a steep truncation immediately beyond a core radius of 20 to 30 kpc, confirming previous studies. MOND reduces the necessary dynamical mass by a factor of 4 to 10. The residual missing mass is proportional to the total gas mass, being roughly twice lower.

articles.title: Comprehensive classification of HCN1 variants linked to neurodevelopmental disorders with and without epilepsy
articles.titleEn: Comprehensive classification of HCN1 variants linked to neurodevelopmental disorders with and without epilepsy
articles.abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated 1 (HCN1) channels mediate the cationic I h current, a fundamental regulator of neuronal excitability and synaptic integration, and are predominantly expressed in the cortex and hippocampus. Although HCN1 variants have been increasingly identified in patients with epilepsy, from milder forms to developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE), genotype–phenotype correlations remain poorly defined. Here, we used patch-clamp electrophysiology and confocal imaging in HEK293 cells to functionally characterize 43 HCN1 variants identified in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders, with or without epilepsy. Based on biophysical properties, we established a classification system comprising four distinct functional classes: I) low or no current; II) hyperpolarizing shift in voltage dependence; III) depolarizing shift in voltage dependence; and IV) generation of an instantaneous current. The molecular basis for this classification was further interpreted using available cryo-EM structures of HCN1. Integration with clinical data from 50 patients revealed a striking correlation between functional class and clinical presentation. Loss-of-function variants prevailed among individuals with milder phenotypes or without epilepsy, with the latter distinctively clustering within the channel selectivity filter. In contrast, gain-of-function and mixed variants were predominantly associated with DEE. Finally, we demonstrate that allosteric modulators, including peptides NB6 and TRIP8b nano and the small molecule J&J12e, effectively normalize channel function across three of the four classes in vitro. These findings establish a biophysical framework for interpreting HCN1 variants, demonstrating that the direction of channel dysfunction is a major determinant of epilepsy risk and severity, and providing a conceptual foundation for future class-based precision medicine approaches.

articles.title: Progressive shifts in soil respiration response to long-term nitrogen enrichment across global forests and grasslands
articles.titleEn: Progressive shifts in soil respiration response to long-term nitrogen enrichment across global forests and grasslands
articles.abstract: Soil stores the largest pool of actively cycling carbon (C) on land, and its dynamics under global changes are critical for projecting climate feedbacks. Global nitrogen (N) deposition has more than doubled since the 1860s; however, the temporal dynamics of soil C emissions under prolonged N deposition are poorly understood. Here, using a global time-series dataset compiled from 38 long-term experiments in forests and grasslands, we find that the response of soil respiration (Rs) to N addition systematically shifts from a transient increase persisting for approximately 2 y to a sustained suppression over time (mean effect = −6%; 95% CI = [−10%, −3%]). Rs in forests and grasslands followed consistent nonlinear trajectories, characterized by a rapid initial decline in the magnitude of the response, which progressively leveled off. Notably, suppression of Rs emerged when cumulative N inputs exceeded a threshold of ~100 kg N ha −1 . Consequently, the suppression was both stronger and occurred more rapidly under high-level N additions (>50 kg N ha −1 y −1 ). These temporal dynamics were associated with N-induced soil acidification and related changes in microbial properties. Overall, these findings indicate that accurate prediction of land–atmosphere C fluxes under global change requires models to capture the reported temporal dynamics.

articles.title: Lead impairs long-term memory by disrupting mitochondrial redox homeostasis in Drosophila
articles.titleEn: Lead impairs long-term memory by disrupting mitochondrial redox homeostasis in Drosophila
articles.abstract: Lead (Pb) exposure remains a major environmental risk factor for cognitive dysfunction, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying Pb-induced memory impairment are poorly understood. Here, we show that both developmental and adult-onset Pb exposure selectively disrupts protein-synthesis-dependent long-term memory (LTM) in Drosophila melanogaster while sparing other memory forms. Using a mitochondria-targeted redox biosensor (mito-roGFP2-Orp1), we found that Pb elevates mitochondrial oxidative stress and disrupts redox homeostasis in cholinergic neurons and in dorsal-anterior-lateral (DAL) neurons, a critical locus for LTM consolidation. Pb-induced redox imbalance suppresses training-induced de novo protein synthesis in DAL neurons, thereby impairing memory consolidation. Antioxidant treatment with epigallocatechin gallate restores mitochondrial redox balance and rescues LTM by reinstating activity-dependent protein synthesis in DAL neurons. These findings identify mitochondrial redox dysregulation as a key mechanism linking environmental Pb exposure to impaired memory consolidation. Our results further establish a genetically tractable platform for dissecting neurotoxic mechanisms and for evaluating antioxidant-based strategies to mitigate Pb-induced cognitive dysfunction.

articles.title: Municipal sludge disposal emerges as a major, hidden, and rapidly growing atmospheric mercury source
articles.titleEn: Municipal sludge disposal emerges as a major, hidden, and rapidly growing atmospheric mercury source
articles.abstract: Wastewater treatment greatly reduces mercury pollution in aquatic ecosystems but does not eliminate it. Here, we identify municipal sludge disposal as a major, long-overlooked atmospheric mercury source. In China, sludge disposal emitted 42 - 10 + 18 Mg in 2024, exceeding 10% of national anthropogenic emissions and ranking third after cement production and nonferrous metal smelting. These emissions have increased by nearly a thousandfold since the 1970s and are concentrated in densely populated urban areas, driven by the rapid expansion of sludge incineration, codisposal, and composting. Our findings reveal a cross-media pollution transfer embedded in sustainability transitions and call for sludge disposal to be incorporated into UNEP mercury budget and Minamata Convention assessments.

articles.title: Revealing the Mechanism of Solute Anomalous Transport Within Discrete Fracture Networks: Insight From Differences in Flow Pathways
articles.titleEn: Revealing the Mechanism of Solute Anomalous Transport Within Discrete Fracture Networks: Insight From Differences in Flow Pathways
articles.abstract: Understanding anomalous solute transport is crucial for effective groundwater contamination prediction and control, and efficient utilization of subsurface oil reservoirs. Variations in fracture pathways within fractured rock masses play a pivotal role in these anomalous behaviors. Traditional models face challenges in capturing complex phenomena, such as early breakthrough, heavy tailing, and multimodality, caused by these variations, highlighting the need for a quantitative, pathway‐resolved understanding of fracture‐network transport responses. In this study, a three‐dimensional discrete fracture network model was constructed from measured fracture data and subsequently converted into an equivalent pipe network for efficient simulation of both flow and solute transport. By identifying complete inlet‐to‐outlet flow pathways and tracing particle trajectories to these pathways, the study quantified the contributions of different pathways to solute transport behaviors. The results show that early arrivals are concentrated in a small number of connected pathways, whereas late arrivals are associated with longer, lower‐velocity connected pathways that contribute to power‐law tailing; parallel pathway groups with substantially different travel times contribute to multimodal behavior. Furthermore, the early breakthrough index ( I EA ) and tailing index ( β BTC ) show systematic correspondence with flow‐conditioned pathway travel‐time characteristics across 200 network realizations. Including variable apertures correlated with trace length further enhances flow focusing, early breakthrough, and tailing. These findings demonstrate that pathway decomposition provides a quantitative means of attributing breakthrough‐curve features to identifiable transport pathways, offering a path‐resolved interpretation of anomalous transport arising from differential advection and hydrodynamic dispersion in complex fracture networks.

articles.title: Atmospheric Stilling Reshapes Algal Blooms and Eutrophication Risk in Shallow Lakes
articles.titleEn: Atmospheric Stilling Reshapes Algal Blooms and Eutrophication Risk in Shallow Lakes
articles.abstract: Atmospheric stilling, defined as long‐term decline in wind speed, has emerged as a widespread climate signal, yet its role as an independent driver of eutrophication in shallow lakes remains poorly understood. Taking Lake Taihu as a representative case, we applied a coupled hydrodynamic‐ecological model (GOTM‐WET) to quantitatively estimate the impacts of declining wind speed on a large shallow lake, while keeping external nutrient loading constant. Model simulations showed that under a strong stilling scenario (45% wind reduction relative to the 2018–2022 baseline), mean surface water temperature increased by 1.96°C, while weakened vertical mixing reduced oxygen transport to bottom waters, resulting in a 56.2% decline in bottom‐water dissolved oxygen (DO). The development of hypoxic conditions intensified sediment anaerobic processes, enhancing internal phosphorus release while simultaneously accelerating denitrification‐driven nitrogen loss. These coupled biogeochemical responses drove a shift toward a phosphorus‐enriched and nitrogen‐depleted nutrient regime, fundamentally altering nutrient limitation patterns. Consequently, surface chlorophyll a (Chl a ) concentrations increased markedly, particularly in summer, with a mean enhancement of 45.4%, accompanied by more persistent and intense algal blooms, indicating pronounced seasonal differences in lake ecosystem responses to declining wind speed. Our results demonstrate that declining wind speeds modulate lake hydrodynamics, oxygen supply, and nutrient structure, driving coupled responses in lake temperature‐nutrient‐phytoplankton systems and markedly increasing the risk of eutrophication, highlighting atmospheric stilling as a previously underappreciated driver of the eutrophication risk in large shallow lakes under future climate change.

articles.title: Continental water storage trends and budgets from the GRACE/GRACE-FO Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product (G3P)
articles.titleEn: Continental water storage trends and budgets from the GRACE/GRACE-FO Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product (G3P)
articles.abstract: The Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product (G3P) provides global groundwater storage (GWS) variations derived from GRACE/GRACE-FO terrestrial water storage (TWS) change by subtracting root-zone soil moisture, glacier mass change, surface water storage, and snow water equivalent. G3P thus provides the first globally consistent, publicly available groundwater dataset from satellite gravimetry for continental-scale water resources assessment. Here, we use G3P to assess global GWS trends over the extended GRACE/GRACE-FO record, jointly with TWS and the subtracted storage components. A central challenge is that apparent long-term trends in GRACE/GRACE-FO water storage records can reflect persistent storage change, natural climate variability, hydrological memory, and observational errors, complicating trend detection and continental-scale storage-change budgets. We address this using a calibrated trend-analysis framework that jointly accounts for trend, seasonal, and stochastic variations in each grid-cell time series. Statistically significant trends are then aggregated to quantify volumetric GWS and TWS gains, losses, and net changes at continental and global scales. Applying this framework to 21.5 years of data (April 2002–September 2023), we find that groundwater depletion is a major contributor to freshwater decline at continental scales, most prominently in Asia (−55 km 3 yr −1 ), while cryospheric mass loss dominates the strongest TWS declines in high-latitude and glacierized regions. Pronounced regional contrasts include increasing groundwater storage across large parts of Africa (+37 km 3 yr −1 ), negative trends in drought-affected regions, and widespread negative or near-threshold GWS tendencies across the Northern Hemisphere. Globally, significance-filtered net GWS and TWS changes are approximately −27 and −183 km 3 yr −1 , respectively. The corresponding gross negative GWS change of approximately 103 km 3 yr −1 is of the same order as model-based estimates of global groundwater depletion. Sensitivity tests indicate robust results: at 95 %, detected area increases by 30 % for TWS and 36 % for GWS, while net-loss magnitudes rise by only 9 % and 18 %. Across much of the seasonal-to-interannual spectral range, GWS is the dominant individual storage-component signal within TWS, which highlights the importance of groundwater for continental freshwater availability.

articles.title: Slope-Constrained Orography (SCO v1.0) for explicit discrete-slope control in terrain preprocessing: a case study with WRF-ARW (v4.6.1)
articles.titleEn: Slope-Constrained Orography (SCO v1.0) for explicit discrete-slope control in terrain preprocessing: a case study with WRF-ARW (v4.6.1)
articles.abstract: Kilometre-scale Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations over terrain with steep slopes often require strong smoothing to prevent numerical instability, but conventional domain-wide filters alter terrain at every grid point, regardless of whether local slopes require reduction. Slope-Constrained Orography (SCO) is an offline terrain preprocessing method that prescribes a target slope angle θ and adjusts only those grid points whose eight-neighbour elevation differences exceed the implied bound, leaving the remaining terrain unchanged. By prescribing the slope constraint directly, SCO provides a geometrically interpretable primary user-facing parameter for terrain construction and stability testing. In a 1 km WRF case over the highly complex terrain of the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, the least-modified stable SCO member among those tested modifies 14 % of points with a mean elevation change of 8.2 m, compared with 100 % modification and 108.1 m for the corresponding WRF Preprocessing System (WPS) member. The successful SCO configuration produces lower near-surface wind and temperature errors in this case.
